chunks: Saad ibn Abdullah al-Ash'ari said: I heard Ahmad ibn Ubaidullah ibn Khaqan, while he was the governor of the ruler in Qom, in a lengthy hadith which we have condensed:

He said: When Abu Muhammad, Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him), fell ill, he sent to my father informing him that Ibn al-Rida had fallen ill. So he mounted quickly and went to the Dar al-Khilafa (House of Caliphate). Then he returned hurriedly with five of the servants of the Commander of the Faithful, from his trusted and special men, one of whom was Nahir. He ordered them to stay at the house of Abu Muhammad and to inquire about his news and condition. He sent for a group of physicians and ordered them to visit him regularly and attend to him morning and evening.

After two days, he was informed that he had grown weak. He mounted and went to see him, then ordered the physicians to stay with him. He sent for the Chief Justice, brought him to his court, and ordered him to choose ten of his companions and sent them to the house of Abu Muhammad, ordering them to stay with him day and night.

They remained there until he passed away on a day from the month of Rabi' al-Awwal in the year 260 AH. The news spread in Samarra that Ibn al-Rida had died. Then they made preparations for him, the markets were closed, my father, the Banu Hashim, and all the people mounted for his funeral. The ruler ordered Abu Isa ibn al-Mutawakkil to offer the funeral prayer for him.

When the bier was placed, Abu Isa approached, uncovered his face, and presented him to the Banu Hashim from the Alawite and Abbasite branches, the commanders, the scribes, the judges, and the just jurists, saying: 'This is Hasan ibn Ali ibn Muhammad ibn al-Rida, who died a natural death on his bed. He was attended by the trusted servants of the Commander of the Faithful, so-and-so and so-and-so and so-and-so.' Then he covered his face and offered the funeral prayer, reciting five Takbirs. He ordered him to be carried, and he was carried from the middle of his house and buried in the house where his father was buried.

key_terms.ابن الرضا: Ibn al-Rida (Son of the Acceptance), a title for Imam Ali al-Hadi (a.s.) used here for his father, or referring to the Imam himself depending on context; in this text, 'Ibn al-Rida' refers to Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) as the son of Ali al-Hadi.
key_terms.دار الخلافة: Dar al-Khilafa (House of Caliphate), the residence of the Abbasid Caliph.
key_terms.ربيع الأول: Rabi' al-Awwal, the third month of the Islamic lunar calendar.
key_terms.صلاة الجنازة: Salat al-Janazah (Funeral Prayer), the ritual prayer performed for the deceased.
key_terms.قاضي القضاة: Qadi al-Qudat (Chief Justice), the head of the judicial system.
key_terms.مات حتف أنفه: Mat hatf anfih (died a natural death), a phrase indicating death without violent or suspicious circumstances.

ai.seo_question: What were the circumstances and witnesses of Imam Hasan al-Askari's death?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the political anxiety surrounding the death of Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.), as the Abbasid caliphate feared the emergence of a hidden successor. The detailed account of the vigil by trusted servants and the public verification by officials underscores the Shia concern over the legitimacy of the Imamate during the period of minor occultation.
